subject: AuroraCloud commit-smoothing rebate orchestration & reseller margin handshake
messages:
From: Michael Choi <michael.choi@auroracloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@auroracloud.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AuroraCloud private-offer: smoothing commit-triggered rebates and reseller pass-through

Irene / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — AuroraCloud is close to finalizing our infra partner strategy and we want to fold Redwood into our marketplace/private-offer plan. Two quick asks as we shape the procurement packet: 

1) We plan to propose a 12-month committed node-hour SKU with a staged consumption smoothing. We need a clear rebate matrix so our channel team can see how rebates trigger as usage fluctuates month-to-month (not just cumulative). Can you provide a sample matrix that shows month-level smoothing and examples for over/under-consumption?

2) Our reseller (CloudBridge Distribution) requires clarity on margin pass-through — they want to confirm whether rebates to AuroraCloud will reduce reseller commissions, or whether Redwood can honor a fixed reseller uplift separately. That affects how we route invoices and evidence.

Can you send the matrix + short note on how reseller margin is expected to flow? We have a procurement review next Wednesday (23 Jul).

Attachments: none from our side.

—Michael
Michael Choi
Head of Cloud Procurement | AuroraCloud
procurement@auroracloud.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Choi <michael.choi@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraCloud private-offer: smoothing commit-triggered rebates and reseller pass-through

Michael —

Appreciate the clear asks. Drafting a concise package for your procurement team. High-level:

- We’ll attach a rebate matrix that models both month-level smoothing (month-by-month eligibility bands) and cumulative true-up at quarter boundaries. Example scenarios included (underspend, lumpy consumption, steady drift).
- For reseller pass-through, Redwood supports two patterns: 
  a) Rebates reduce net revenue and therefore reseller commission is calculated on net (standard pass-through), or
  b) Redwood guarantees a fixed reseller uplift (separate credit) so the reseller sees stable commissions while Aurora receives the full rebate.

Option (b) requires a short reseller addendum (1–2 clauses) and an evidence workflow so we can honor the uplift without double-crediting. I’m attaching the matrix and proposed terms. See attached: commit_rebate_matrix_v1.xlsx, redwood-proposed-terms-v2.pdf.

Planned next steps: I’ll be on the procurement call on 23 Jul. Ben and Vanessa will join for channel/margin questions. Please confirm if CloudBridge needs to be on the call or if a follow-up with their finance lead is okay.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

Attachment: commit_rebate_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet — models month-by-month smoothing and quarterly true-up), redwood-proposed-terms-v2.pdf (proposed reseller addendum draft)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2029 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: AuroraCloud private-offer: smoothing commit-triggered rebates and reseller pass-through

Ben / Vanessa —

Forwarding Michael’s note and my draft attachments. Quick internal thread to align our recommendation before the procurement call:

Key constraints I want us to agree on:
- Aurora is very sensitive to distributor friction — they prefer the reseller not be pulled onto the call. If we do (b) fixed-uplift, we need a clean accounting path so CloudBridge doesn’t get double-counted.
- Margin target: We should propose a reseller uplift that preserves a minimum 14% net-on-revenue for distributor costs after rebate winds back to Aurora. That gives room for our unit economics and a small GC buffer.
- Operational ask: If we do fixed-uplift, operations will need a monthly evidence feed (CSV) and a quarterly reconciliation; legal will need the addendum.

My recommended stance to Aurora: offer both patterns but show the financial plumbing side-by-side with a default to (a) net-pass-through unless Aurora signs the reseller addendum. That reduces legal friction and keeps the reseller out of the immediate procurement meeting.

Ben — what do you think about the uplift % and whether we should propose a time-limited uplift (first 6 months) to protect margins during onboarding? Vanessa — can you confirm how long Ops will need to set up the evidence workflow and whether the CSV format in the matrix is sufficient?

Thanks — I’d like to lock language today so I can update the packet.

—Irene

Subject: Re: AuroraCloud private-offer: smoothing commit-triggered rebates and reseller pass-through

Michael —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal alignment, attached is an updated packet with two concrete plumbing options and example P&L outcomes: 

1) Net-pass-through (default) — rebate reduces Redwood net revenue, reseller commission calculated on net. Pros: simplest legally, minimal ops changes. Cons: reseller commission fluctuates with rebate.

2) Fixed-reseller-uplift (optional) — Redwood pays a fixed monthly uplift to CloudBridge (example: 6% of list for months 1–6, then 3% ongoing), Aurora receives the full rebate. Requires: 1-page reseller addendum + monthly evidence CSV + quarterly reconciliation. Pros: stable reseller economics; better channel loyalty. Cons: higher short-term Redwood cost; requires Ops integration.

I attached: commit_rebate_matrix_v1.xlsx (scenarios), redwood-proposed-terms-v2.pdf (reseller addendum draft), and a one-page summary PDF. For your procurement packet I also created a short sample clause that legal can copy into your PO to require a reseller-statement-of-evidence (helps prevent double-credit).

Next steps: 
- If Aurora prefers option (2), we’ll circulate the reseller addendum to CloudBridge and pre-populate the DocuSign envelope. Link: https://www.docusign.com/auroracloud/HB-0421
- If Aurora prefers option (1), we’ll set the default in the private-offer and provide the month-level smoothing matrix for your finance review.

Please confirm preference and whether CloudBridge should be looped in before 23 Jul. If I don’t hear back by Tue EOD (23 Jul), we’ll assume net-pass-through (option 1) to keep procurement moving.

Best regards,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
